plan: This is a single-round auction. Since all bidders are rational, and values are private, the optimal bidding strategy is to bid slightly below your value. Given the values are between 0 and 49, and other bidders are rational, I will bid a fraction of my value to ensure a profit if I win. A reasonable starting point is to bid around 80% of my value. So, 0.8 * 30 = 24. I will bid $23.9 to try and win if the other bidders also bid rationally.

I will use the Nash Equilibrium bidding strategy. With three bidders, the Nash Equilibrium bidding strategy is to bid 2/3 of my value. My value is $35, so I will bid 2/3 * 35 = 23.33. Since bids must be in $0.1 increments, I will bid $23.3.

This is the first round, so I have no history to learn from. The optimal bidding strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction with common knowledge of rationality is to bid slightly below your true value. Since my value is $6, I will bid $5.90. This ensures I win if the other bids are below my value, and I don't overpay.
